newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond spreads steady amid some selling.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond spreads steady amid some selling.

text.p: Moderate U.S. corporate bond selling and the promise of $2.0 billion in supply failed to unseat fragile sentiments and spreads finished little changed on Tuesday, traders said.

J.C. Penney Cos five-tranche deal, expected to price on Wednesday, was seen issue-bid for most parts throughout the session. Some traders said prices may waft to the wider side of price talk for the longer tranches, including the 30-year debt and 40-year putable bonds.
Spreads were not affected by the size of the deal thanks to the otherwise thin new issue slate, traders said.

The deal is expected to include $600 million five-year debt priced between 45 and 50 basis points over the curve; $400 million 10-year debt at 70 basis points over; $300 million 20-year bonds at 85 basis points over; $350 million 30-year non-call 10 debt at 120 basis points over; and $350 million 40-year put 10 bonds in the mid-40 basis point range.
Reflecting the cautious tone, some of the issue-bids were hit and then backed up in the next round, one trader said.
"The deal is going to do okay," one trader said. "People aren't screaming buyers in here but J.C. Penney does not have a lot of competitition and it'll get done.
Dealers noted the investor desire for putable bonds is significantly lower in a rising interest rate environment.
The deal will be priced on Wednesday via a syndicate led by Credit Suisse First Boston.

Elsewhere, a large corporate bid list from Gruntal & Co was absorbed without much talk of indigestion and spreads were pressured minimally. Prices in the broad market mirrored the back-up in U.S. Treasuries, traders said.

Turning to the high-yield market, dealers reported a mixed price environment with bigger buyers still reluctant, or unable, to bid prices higher. Prices were marginally firmer on a spread basis as the Treasury market fell, they added.
Cheaply priced new issues traded up in the secondary.

Bway Corp's $100 million 10-1/4 percent 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced at par via a BT Securities Corp syndicate, were bid above 101 when freed. Sterling Chemicals Inc's $150 million 11-1/4 percent debt was unchanged but still higher from its par issue price.
